arm-A.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
arm-A.summary: Four cops breach Room 303 of the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she submits slowly, hands behind her head. Outside, Agent Smith corrects the Lieutenant's belief that the raid is succeeding, telling him his two units are already dead. Back in the room, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity moves: she breaks the arrest and kills the squad in a blur of inhuman speed, leaving herself the only one standing as a flashlight rocks to stillness.
arm-A.action: The raid that looked like a clean collar is revealed to have been a trap closing on the cops, not on her.

arm-B.title: Trinity's capture turns into a massacre
arm-B.summary: Four cops breach Room 303 in the fire-gutted Heart O' The City Hotel and take Trinity at gunpoint; she raises her hands behind her head in apparent surrender. Outside, the Lieutenant brags that his units are bringing down 'one little girl' while Agent Smith tells him those men are already dead. Back inside, the moment the Big Cop reaches with the cuffs, Trinity moves inhumanly fast: she shatters his nose and hurls him across the room into another cop, killing them both, snatches a gun, twists it, and fires. When the gunfire ends, one flashlight rocks slowly to a stop over the dead and Trinity is the only one standing, unhurt. She lets slip a single 'Shit.' Outside, Smith turns and heads into the hotel on Smith's nod, leaving the defiant, disbelieving Lieutenant behind.
arm-B.action: The raid on Room 303 inverts in a single instant. Trinity's surrender in the room is a choice, not a defeat: she lets the squad believe the arrest is routine, then converts the first physical contact — the Big Cop's cuffs reaching for her — into the opening of her violence. She breaks the perimeter, turns the cops' own momentum and weapons against them, and by the end has wiped out the armed, outnumbering squad, standing alone over the dead as the victor rather than the captive. Outside the hotel, the Agents already know the outcome and move to seize the operation while the Lieutenant, still believing his men are succeeding, rages against them in denial.

arm-A.title: Trinity's escape across the rooftops to the phone
arm-A.summary: Informed that her hotel hardline is dead and that Agents are on site, Trinity drops the phone and runs for a separate pay phone at Wells and Lake. She slips past Agent Brown's unit in the hall onto the fire escape, is forced upward when Agent Smith blocks the alley, and crosses the rooftops with impossible grace while the cops fall behind and Brown matches her leap. She dives through a window into a back stairwell, crashes down injured but still moving, finds no pursuer behind her, then races a garbage truck to a ringing phone and answers it a split-second before the truck destroys the booth, leaving no body.

arm-A.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-A.summary: Alone in his technology-crammed apartment, Neo is jolted from sleep by his own PC typing messages at him that end with a real knock answering the screen, leaving him unable to tell whether he was awake or dreaming. He still closes a disk-for-cash deal with Choi through his chained, multi-locked door, but the visit leaves him hollowed by a returning sense of unrealness, and when Dujour proposes taking him out he refuses until he spots a small white rabbit pin on her jacket, at which the room seems to tilt and he agrees. At a smoke-filled gathering of people dressed in black, Trinity walks straight up to him, names herself as the hacker who was on his computer, warns him that he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless solitude as a search for a hidden figure and an answer no one can be told. Pressing close in the deafening music, she withholds the substance and instead gives him the question, which he finally voices aloud before she melts back into the crowd, leaving him with the promise that the answer is out there and will find him.
arm-A.action: Neo is woken at his PC by messages that type themselves on his screen and end with a knock that answers the last line, cracking his cause-and-effect certainty and blurring the machine into the real. He performs normalcy, opening his series of locks and chain to complete a disk-for-cash deal with Choi, then is left hollowed by a recurring wave of unrealness. He refuses Dujour's offer to go out until the white rabbit pin on her jacket flips him into motion, and he arrives at the party out of place, beer in hand. Trinity approaches, names herself as the one who was on his computer, warns him he is being watched and in danger, and turns his private, sleepless obsession into a directed search, pressing close in the loud music until he voices What is the Matrix? and is told the answer can only be seen, not explained. She then withdraws into the shifting crowd, leaving him alone with the question and the promise that the answer will find him.

arm-B.title: Neo is summoned and drawn toward the truth
arm-B.summary: Alone in his apartment, Neo is contacted through his own machine by an unseen party that types messages on its own, answers a knock with the last line, and tells him to follow a white rabbit. When Choi and Dujour arrive for a disk deal, Neo spots a white rabbit pin on Dujour's jacket, and against his plan to work the next day he agrees to go out. At a crowded apartment gathering, Trinity approaches him by name, confirms she was on his computer, catalogs his private habits to prove she has been watching, warns him he is in danger and being watched, and reframes his sleepless searching as the hunt for an answer that is out there and will find him if he wants it, though it must be seen to be believed. She draws him in with a hypnotic, unhurried closeness over the deafening music, then melts back into the crowd, leaving him on his feet in the night, having named aloud the question What is the Matrix?.
arm-B.action: The screens in Neo's apartment go blank and type messages on their own, answering a knock with the last line; Neo trades a disk to Choi for money, then follows Dujour out after recognizing the white rabbit pin; at the gathering, Trinity corners him against a wall and delivers a warning before disappearing into the crowd.

arm-A.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that forces are closing in. Neo peeks over the partition and spots Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones guiding a cluster of officers, while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down he moves down the line until he reaches the first office on the left side. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken in her rearview mirror.

state_triples.reading: Smith moves through the office as though the outcome is already decided — he enters Neo's cubicle himself rather than delegate, because he does not conceive of a way out of a sealed floor. That certainty is exactly what Neo exploits to get behind him, but it costs Smith nothing: his patience and his net are large enough that one evasion changes nothing. He is conducting, not chasing, and the capture at the end is the vindication of that composure rather than a relief.

Trinity's single curse is the measure of how much rests on Neo's escape — she is placed exactly where she can see it fail. Her dismay is not surprise at the raid but at its outcome: the man she has been steering toward the truth has been taken, and she can do nothing but witness it. The restraint of the reaction — one word, seen in a mirror

Her single gesture — turning and pointing out Neo's cubicle the instant the Agents arrive — is legible to everyone in the room but her own motive stays hidden, and that ambiguity is the whole point. She may be a knowing collaborator handing Neo over, or simply a startled coworker redirecting a frightening commotion toward its source; the scene refuses to decide, and so does Neo, who cannot tell whether he has been incidentally exposed or deliberately betrayed.

Morpheus guides with the calm of someone who has been waiting for this moment and means to use it — he tests Neo's readiness even in the middle of a raid, withholding explanation ('The answer is coming') and refusing to soothe beyond the facts. At the ledge he does not command; he lays out the two ways out and hands Neo the choice, then hangs up, because he believes fear, not incapacity

The phone is Neo's only tether to the one person trying to get him out, and its fall is the event's quiet turning point: from the moment it rings at his desk it is his lifeline, clutched through every command, and when the wind knocks it from his hand on the ledge he loses not just his balance but his guide. Its loss is what leaves him alone to decide — and alone to fail.

arm-A.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
arm-A.summary: The Agents close in on Neo in the interrogation room. Smith lays out Neo's two lives and offers to wipe his record clean in exchange for Morpheus; Neo refuses with contempt, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. arm-B.title: Neo is interrogated and implanted
arm-B.summary: In a white interrogation room, Agent Smith reads Neo the contents of his file and offers to wipe his crimes clean in exchange for Morpheus's location. Neo refuses with contempt, gives Smith the finger, and demands a phone call. When Smith asks what good a call is if he cannot speak, Neo's lips meld together until his mouth is gone. Neo lunges for the door; the standing Agents pin him to the chair and tear open his shirt, and Smith drives a fiber-optic tap that has become a living insect-worm creature into his navel, where it burrows inside him as he panics and struggles.
arm-B.action: The scene opens on Neo seated whole-bodied and defiant in the room. Smith sits across from him, lays down the manila file labeled "Anderson, Thomas A.", and runs through Neo's two lives before offering to wipe the slate clean for Morpheus. Neo rejects the bargain, insults Smith, and demands his phone call. Smith removes his sunglasses to show ice-blue eyes and asks what use a call is if Neo cannot speak; Neo's lips fuse smooth. Neo lunges for the door, the standing Agents seize and hold him down while Smith rips his shirt open, and Smith withdraws a fiber-optic wire that animates into a living creature and drives it into Neo's navel, where it burrows in as Neo struggles helplessly.

His demand for a phone call is a category error, an appeal to rules that do not apply to the being across the table, and the violation that.

arm-A.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
arm-A.summary: Waking from a nightmare that left him mouthless with a creature lodged in his abdomen, Neo is reached by a tapped phone on which Morpheus names him 'the One,' tells him Morpheus has spent his life searching for him, warns that the danger is himself, and wins his reluctant '... Yes' before hanging up. Trinity then pulls up beside him at The Adams Street bridge and gets him into a car, where Switch holds him at gunpoint and the crew means to run a steel-and-glass device on him. Neo tries to bolt, but Trinity's appeal to a road he already knows stops him, and he closes the car door and lets them take him on through the wet dark toward Morpheus — committing without trusting his captors.

His '... Yes' is spoken from vertigo, not conviction, and his final act, closing the car door, is the same reflex dressed up as agency: he chooses the abyss he recognizes over the one he cannot see. arm-B.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
arm-B.summary: A ringing phone wakes Neo — mouthless, shirt torn open, an implanted creature burrowing inside him — and a voice names him 'the One' and demands a single 'Yes.' He walks to the Adams Street bridge in the pouring rain, where a car slides to a stop; inside, Switch holds him at gunpoint while Apoc drives and Trinity insists the restraint is 'for our protection. From you.' When Switch stops the car and lays down 'Our way or the highway,' Neo opens the door to bolt, but Trinity reframes his flight as a road he has already been down and where it ends, and he closes the door and stays. The car then rushes off through the dark, wet streets, Neo half-dressed and rain-soaked, handed over to a war he has just consented to enter.
arm-B.action: Morpheus calls Neo from a tapped line, warns him the Agents reached him first, declares him 'the One,' and extracts a '... Yes' before directing him to the Adams Street bridge. On that bridge a car slides to a stop and Trinity orders him in; inside, Switch holds him at gunpoint while Apoc drives and Trinity insists the restraint is 'for our protection. From you.' Switch stops the car and lays down 'Our way or the highway.' Neo opens the door to bolt, but Trinity appeals to a road he has already been down and where it ends, and he closes the door and stays. The car then rushes through the dark, wet streets toward whatever waits.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being claimed by a destiny he never asked for and cannot yet comprehend. Each authority — the phone, the gun, the steel device — promises him a future that requires surrender, and each time his only real choice is how to frame the capitulation. He answers '... Yes' from vertigo, not conviction, and closes the car door not because he trusts Trinity but because the road she names is a fall he recognizes.
